output.name: Kessal
output.myth: Before the cut, Kessal was a fisher's wife who would not leave the kelp pool when the ebb ran out. Her man called to her from the boat. She lifted one foot, then the other, and could not set either down again. Mother Hesk, who keeps count of everything that stands still, wound her into the Lamp Road as a mark. Aun laughed from the sky and said a post is no use to a net, then looked west at the Cut Kite, where his own kites still ran after the sky. Tavo came down the cliff and shook the water off her wings, and still she did not move. Tavo laughed at the Hat the Gale Kept in the north-east and forgot her. Kael has cast for her many times and never caught her, because she has not fallen. She is only waiting for the water to turn. Whoever stands that long at a pool is said to get the best fish. Old women say this is true. Old women have also stood that long, and the fish were not the point.
output.finding: Find the Cut Kite on the Lamp Road and look one hand-span (about 20°) east of it, where the Mooring Post stands alone.
